passage:
Monday. Raghav told Hemant, a classmate from his lab batch, that he didn't like being grabbed by the shoulders and asked him to stop. Hemant laughed and said it was just a joke.

Wednesday. In the corridor Hemant grabbed Raghav's arm again. Raghav raised his palm and said firmly, "No. Don't touch me." Hemant kept his hand there for a second. Raghav pulled his arm free with a light push and stepped away, heart racing, and walked into the staff room.

Friday. Raghav met the department counsellor and reported what had happened, with the dates. The counsellor listened, thanked him for telling them, and said they would speak to Hemant and the head. Raghav felt shaky, but lighter.

qa.q: Whom did Raghav report to on Friday?
qa.a: Raghav reported to the department counsellor.

qa.q: What was Raghav feeling as he walked into the staff room?
qa.a: Raghav was frightened and angry, and his racing heart shows it. He also chose a safe place to go rather than reacting back.

qa.q: What steps did Raghav take that protected him?
qa.a: He said no clearly, raised a palm, pulled free and stepped away, then reported it to the counsellor with dates.

qa.q: How might Hemant have seen the first request?
qa.a: Hemant treated it as a joke and did not stop, which shows he ignored the clear boundary rather than misunderstanding it.

grounding: A young adult sets a boundary with a firm no, a raised palm and a step away, and when ignored leaves and reports.

passage: Jaya, come and sit. I want to tell you something from when I was twenty. There was a boy in my hostel, Deepak, who liked to put his arm around every girl's shoulder. I told him once, politely, "Please don't." He just grinned. So the next time I put my hand up flat, stepped back and said, "I said no." My knees were shaking, but my voice wasn't. He went red and let go. I still went to the warden that evening and told her, because one no isn't always enough. I'm Uma, and I've learned that you never owe anyone your comfort. Step away, say it clearly, and tell someone you trust.

qa.q: What did Uma do with her hand when she said no the second time?
qa.a: Uma put her hand up flat and stepped back.

qa.q: What was Uma feeling when she said 'I said no'?
qa.a: Uma was frightened, as her shaking knees show, but she was also determined and kept her voice steady. Deepak's going red shows he understood the boundary.

qa.q: What could a young person do if someone ignores a clear no?
qa.a: Step away, say it again clearly, and tell a trusted person such as a warden, teacher or counsellor.

qa.q: How might Jaya feel hearing this story?
qa.a: Jaya may feel reassured that saying no is allowed, or nervous about speaking up, so hearing that Uma's knees shook too may help.

grounding: An elder recalls setting a boundary with a raised palm and a firm no, and going to a trusted person when it was ignored.

passage: The 6:40 local was so packed that Irawati could barely lift her arm to hold the rail. At Dadar more people pushed in, and a man behind her pressed closer than the crowd needed. His hand brushed her waist, then stayed. Irawati's whole body went cold. There was nowhere to step. She turned her head and said, loud and firm, "Move your hand. Now." He didn't. She shoved his wrist away hard with her elbow. Her friend Keerthana, two people away, saw her face and forced her way over. "Stand with me," Keerthana said, pulling Irawati against the door, her own body between them. At the next station they got down, and Keerthana waved over the railway police constable on the platform. Irawati described the man's shirt and the coach number. The constable radioed ahead. Irawati's hands were shaking, but she felt proud she had said it out loud.

qa.q: At which station did more people push in?
qa.a: At Dadar.

qa.q: What was Irawati feeling when the man's hand stayed on her waist?
qa.a: She felt frightened, her body going cold; afterwards her hands shook, but she also felt proud that she had spoken out loud.

qa.q: Which steps helped Irawati once the man ignored her no?
qa.a: Pushing his wrist away, moving next to Keerthana, getting off at the next station and reporting to the railway police with the details.

qa.q: How did Keerthana react when she saw Irawati's face?
qa.a: She forced her way over, put herself between Irawati and the man, and got the constable, showing she took it seriously.

grounding: Shows a young adult using a firm no and a push to get free of unwanted touch in a crowded train, then leaving and reporting when ignored.

passage: At the office party in Gurugram, Nilesh from accounts kept draping his arm over Rehana's shoulder while telling stories, laughing loudly. The first time she slid out from under it. The second time she stepped back. The third time, she turned to face him, raised one palm between them and said clearly, "Please don't put your arm on me." The group went quiet. Nilesh's face went red. He lifted his arm away at once. "Oh. Sorry, sorry. I didn't realise." He took a step back and put his hands in his pockets. Rehana's heart was hammering, but she nodded. "Thanks." Later he came up to her near the snacks and said, "I'm used to my friends from college. I should have asked. It won't happen again." Rehana said, "Okay," and meant it, though she stayed at the other end of the room for the rest of the evening.

qa.q: What did Rehana raise between them when she spoke?
qa.a: One palm.

qa.q: What was Rehana feeling when she spoke up the third time?
qa.a: She was nervous, her heart hammering, but determined; afterwards she seemed relieved and still a little wary, staying at the other end of the room.

qa.q: What did Nilesh do right once Rehana set the boundary?
qa.a: He stopped at once, stepped back, apologised without arguing, and later took responsibility instead of making excuses.

qa.q: How might the people in the group have seen the moment?
qa.a: They went quiet, likely surprised; seeing Nilesh stop at once may have shown them that a clear no should be respected immediately.

grounding: Shows a young adult using a raised palm, a step away and a firm request to set a boundary, and the other person stopping at once.

passage:
"Your left elbow is dropping," Jagdish said, reaching for Mahima's arm.
"You can just tell me," Mahima said, stepping back. "I'd rather you didn't touch me to correct it."
"It's faster this way. All trainers do it."
"I know. I'm still asking you not to."
He laughed. "Relax, madam." His hand went to her lower back to push her posture.
Mahima twisted away and pushed his hand off. "No. I said no."
"Okay, okay, so sensitive."
Mahima put the dumbbells down. She picked up her bag and walked to the front desk.
"I want to speak to the manager," she told the receptionist, voice shaking a little. "The trainer touched me after I asked him not to."
The manager came out within a minute. "Thank you for telling me. I'm taking him off your sessions from today, and I'll note it formally. Would you like a different trainer?"
"Yes," Mahima said. "One who listens."

qa.q: Where did Mahima go after putting the dumbbells down?
qa.a: She walked to the front desk.

qa.q: What was Mahima feeling when she went to the front desk?
qa.a: She was upset and shaken, her voice shaking a little, but determined to report it after her no was ignored.

qa.q: Which choice worked when Jagdish ignored Mahima's request?
qa.a: Pushing his hand off, leaving the session and reporting to the manager worked, since the manager removed him and noted it formally.

qa.q: How did the gym manager respond, and why does that matter?
qa.a: The manager thanked Mahima, took Jagdish off her sessions that day and noted it, showing her report was taken seriously.

grounding: Shows a young adult setting a touch boundary, pushing away when it is ignored, and leaving and reporting it.

passage: I'm Farida, and I still replay the college fest night, though less than I used to. We were dancing near the stage when a guy I didn't know slid his hand onto my waist. I turned, raised my palm between us and said, loud and flat, "No." Then I stepped back. He grinned and reached again, as if it were a game. I pushed his hand off hard and walked away, straight to Aparna, who was by the water stall. One look at my face and she didn't ask questions; she just came with me. We went to the volunteer desk, where the faculty coordinator, Dr Sen, listened to everything and wrote it down. Within ten minutes two security staff had found him near the stage and walked him out, and Dr Sen offered to help me file a formal complaint the next morning. I did. Saying no didn't feel rude. It felt like mine.

qa.q: Where was Aparna when Farida walked away?
qa.a: By the water stall.

qa.q: What does Farida's walk straight to Aparna suggest about how Farida felt?
qa.a: Farida was likely shaken and angry after the second grab, wanting safety and a friend close; Aparna could read it on Farida's face.

qa.q: Which steps protected Farida after the firm no was ignored?
qa.a: Pushing the hand off, leaving, going to a friend and reporting at the volunteer desk, where the coordinator acted that night and a formal complaint followed.

qa.q: How did Aparna read the moment, and how did she respond?
qa.a: Aparna saw from Farida's face that something was wrong and chose to go along without asking questions, offering quiet support first.

grounding: It illustrates a young adult setting a boundary with a firm no, a raised palm and a step back, pushing free when it is ignored, then leaving and reporting.
